Title: Melaka polls: 25 investigation papers referred to DPP
Article:
MELAKA: Police have referred 25 investigation papers involving various offences during the 2026 Melaka state election to the Deputy Public Prosecutor's Office.
Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said police had received 37 reports and opened 28 investigation papers so far.
"Most of the reports involved vandalism of campaign materials, which are being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code," he told reporters while observing the voting process at the Ayer Molek state constituency polling centre at SK Bendahara Seri Maharaja.
Dzulkhairi said voting at all 240 polling centres, involving 1,213 channels, was proceeding peacefully, with no incidents reported as of 9am.
He said the school was one of seven polling centres in Ayer Molek, with 43 voting channels in total.
He said 3,332 policemen had been deployed for the state election, with another 300 traffic personnel, Federal Reserve Unit (FRU) personnel, including reinforcements from Negri Sembilan, and members of Melaka's Public Order Riot Unit (PORU) also involved in the operation.
Earlier, Dzulkhairi's wife, Datin Diana Aini Mokter, also cast her vote at the polling centre.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: 28.8 per cent turnout recorded as of 11.05am
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 28.8 per cent of ordinary eligible voters in the Melaka election had cast their ballots as of 11.05am today.
According to the Election Commission's (EC) real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring (VTO) dashboard, 194,871 voters had cast their ballots by then.
The dashboard showed that Kesidang recorded the highest turnout among the 28 state constituencies, at 32.7 per cent.
The EC is targeting a 70 per cent turnout for the election, which sees 79 candidates contesting 28 seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Student spends RM700 on air tickets to cast first vote
Article:
KOTA MELAKA: A 20-year-old university student spent RM700 on return flight tickets from Sarawak to Melaka so she could fulfil her responsibility as a first-time voter in the 16th Melaka election today.
Ashira Dania Mohd Hairun, a first-year Social Sciences student at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (Unimas), returned to her hometown in Taman Seri Duyong 2 here to cast her ballot.
She said she was excited to vote for the first time, as it was her first opportunity to choose her elected representative.
"I spent about RM700 on return flight tickets.
"I woke up about 6.30am after my parents woke me up to go and vote.
"My older sister, relatives and a cousin who is also voting for the first time accompanied me today," she said after casting her ballot for the Duyong seat at SK Seri Duyong here.
On her hopes for the elected representative, Ashira said she wanted to see further development in the constituency, as well as more opportunities for young people to participate in community programmes.
"I want Duyong to become more developed and for more young people to take part in any programmes organised by the state constituency. This would allow more of them to get involved in activities here," she said.
She also hoped more youth activities would be organised, particularly in sports such as football, rugby, fishing and netball.
"To Gen Z, go out and vote now. Do not wait until noon. Do not sleep until the afternoon and wait for your parents to scold you before going out to vote. Go out and vote now," she said.
The Duyong seat is seeing a straight fight between Barisan Nasional  incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abd Halem and Pakatan Harapan's Poo Long Suan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Uncle Wong, 88, cycles to polling centre after 3am start
Article:
MELAKA: Eager to fulfil his duty as a voter, Vong Fook Hoi, better known as Uncle Wong, 88, woke up about 3am and cycled to the polling centre at SK Seri Duyong here today.
Uncle Wong said he had woken up as early as 3am because he was so eager to cast his vote that he had difficulty sleeping the night before.
"I woke up at 3am because I could not wait to vote. I could not sleep last night either.
"I came to the polling centre on my bicycle. I go everywhere by bicycle," he said after casting his ballot for the Duyong seat here today.
He said it had taken him longer than usual to leave for the polling centre this time as he had waited for his wife before setting off.
On their responsibility as voters, Uncle Wong said his children had also returned from Singapore and Kuala Lumpur to cast their ballots.
"I have already reminded them. My children are grown up and they know what they need to do," he said.
The Duyong seat is being contested by Barisan Nasional candidate and incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abd Halem and Pakatan Harapan's Poo Long Suan.
The Election Commission's electoral roll recorded 26,528 registered voters in Duyong, an increase of 8,291 from the 18,237 recorded in the 2021 Melaka election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump not expected to raise Alice Huang case with China's Xi
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is not expected to discuss with Chinese President Xi Jinping the case involving a businesswoman whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised national security concerns, US officials said on Friday.
Trump is set to meet with Xi next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, as part of a four-day trip to Asia. The meeting will come just days after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, capping a spectacular fall from the chip industry's heights.
Though semiconductors have been a major flash point in US-China relations, the US president is not expected to raise the latest issue with Xi for now, the officials said,
"When it comes to some of these national security matters and examinations and investigations that are going on in the US, it's probably not something that we're going to read the Chinese in on at this moment," one senior administration official told reporters.
A second US official added: "I don't expect the president to raise it, the Alice Huang issue."
The officials were responding to a reporter's question about whether Trump would raise the allegations involving Alice Huang with Xi.
On Tuesday, the independent members of Nvidia's board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after the New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Jensen Huang's relations with the businesswoman, Alice Huang, as well as US authorities' suspicions that she was spying for China.
Beijing has denied she is a spy. Alice Huang could not be reached. Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government. The Justice Department has said it has not reached any conclusion about Alice Huang's affiliation with the Chinese government.
Jensen Huang apologised in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International. The two are not related.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Wheelchair no barrier to 70-year-old Yusuf fulfilling his voting duty [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: Being wheelchair-bound did not stop 70-year-old Yusuf Taib from fulfilling his responsibility as a voter in the Melaka election today.
For him, age and physical limitations were no excuse to miss the opportunity to cast his ballot and have a say in choosing the state's next government.
Yusuf, who has been voting since before Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad first became prime minister in 1981, said his enthusiasm for exercising his democratic right had never faded.
"I have been voting since before Mahathir became prime minister.
"The spirit to come out and vote is still there, regardless of who comes into power or who leaves," he said after casting his ballot at SK Jalan Datuk Palembang.
The school is one of the polling centres for the Bukit Katil state constituency.
Yusuf said he had been using a wheelchair for the past 15 years after a fall injured his hip, leaving him unable to walk independently.
Although he can still stand for short periods, he said his condition had made it difficult for him to move around without assistance.
An early riser, Yusuf said he had been awake since 5am to perform his morning prayers before leaving home at about 6.30am.
"I usually wake up at 5am and leave the house by 6.30am, or 7am at the latest.
"I enjoy sitting by the roadside and watching cars pass by," he said with a laugh.
Despite his age, Yusuf said the responsibility of choosing the state's leadership should not be taken lightly, particularly by younger voters.
However, he believed that the decision to vote, and whom to support, should ultimately rest with each individual.
"If you want to choose your leaders, then come out and vote. Choose whoever you prefer.
"It is entirely up to each individual. We cannot force anyone to vote for one person or another," he said.
Asked about his hopes for the election outcome, Yusuf declined to speculate on which party would emerge victorious.
Instead, he expressed a simple wish for the next state administration: to govern fairly and look after the welfare of the people, regardless of their political affiliations.
In Bukit Katil, incumbent Adly Zahari of Pakatan Harapan is facing Pas candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif, Bersama candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Woman flies home from Australia to vote with elderly parents
Article:
MELAKA: Distance proved no barrier to civic duty as 38-year-old Wong Chea Fann returned from Australia this morning to cast her ballot alongside her elderly parents at SJK (C) Malim for the Kesidang state seat.
Wong, together with her parents, Wong Heng Hoe, 79, and Lee Cheng Tee, 70, were among the early voters who arrived at the polling centre at 9am.
Wong said she had felt a little nervous at first, but described the morning's atmosphere as exciting rather than stressful.
"It's quite exciting, but most importantly, my parents arrived safely to vote," she said.
She encouraged fellow Melakans to cast their votes before the 5pm deadline.
"It's your future," she said.
For Lee, the priority was having her family together at the polling centre.
"At least my daughter came back from Perth to vote," she said, adding that the voting process was calm and orderly.
"I was even able to catch up with old friends who also turned up in the morning.
"If you care for the place where you live and want it to be peaceful, you should know what to do. Whoever you think can work and is helpful to the country, vote for them," she added.
Kesidang has the largest electorate among Melaka's 28 state seats, with 54,910 registered voters.
The urban constituency is witnessing a three-cornered contest involving incumbent assemblyman Allex Seah Shoo Chin of Pakatan Harapan, Perikatan Nasional's Albert Kok Boon Chang and Bersama's Dr Bryan Kek Kit Hun.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US reopens airspace after nationwide flight halt, rules out cyberattack
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation's airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now "opened up," while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.
"At 8.15 tonight Eastern Time, we've opened up the airspace," Duffy said. "Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It's going to be slow."
The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for US$30 billion to upgrade and modernise the US Air Traffic Control System.
"Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down," Duffy said. "It's the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?"
Duffy however insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide.
"Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump," Mullin said.
Mullin added there was "actually no cyber attack."
"When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, 'Hey, we did that.' There's no chatter.' We haven't seen any footprints," he added.
But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out.
The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began.
"President Trump immediately had people in his office," Mullin said. "We were communicating."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Roque: Asean must turn economic commitments into gains for businesses, people
Article:
MANILA: Asean must back its economic integration plans with clear milestones and consistent implementation to deliver benefits for businesses, consumers and workers, Philippine Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque said.
She said the Asean Economic Community (AEC) Strategic Plan 2026-2030 required effective coordination, while unfinished priority economic deliverables under the Philippines' chairmanship needed to be completed and sustained beyond this year.
"The real measure of this plan will not be the number of commitments we make, but the value they add to every business, consumer, worker, and community.
"The purpose of our work is to make economic integration meaningful in the lives of our people.
"Every commitment we advance should help create opportunities, strengthen livelihoods, and build confidence in our shared future," she said when opening the 28th AEC Council Meeting here on Saturday.
Malaysia's Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani also attended the meeting.
[[nid:1577284]]
Roque outlined three priorities for the council's discussions: reviewing the Philippines' priority economic deliverables, advancing implementation of the AEC Strategic Plan 2026–2030 and finalising reports and outcomes for the upcoming Asean summit.
She said the council's final meeting under the Philippine chairmanship provided an opportunity to assess progress, identify outstanding work and agree on the next steps.
"As we finalise our reports and outcomes for the summit, let us give our leaders a clear picture of where Asean stands, the challenges we must address, and the opportunities we should pursue together," she said.
Roque thanked member states, Asean sectoral bodies and the Asean Secretariat for their cooperation throughout the year, including their readiness to find common ground in advancing regional economic integration.
The meeting precedes the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, scheduled for Nov 15 to 17 in Manila under the Philippines' chairmanship theme, "Navigating Our Future, Together". — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ICC closes original Afghanistan war crimes investigation
Article:
ISTANBUL: Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) have ordered the formal closure of the court's original investigation into alleged crimes in Afghanistan, which included allegations against US troops, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
A separate investigation into alleged crimes by the Taliban since August 2021 will continue.
The Chamber said the prosecution had not demonstrated that it could "effectively carry out any further investigative or prosecutorial activities" in the original Afghanistan investigation, according to a court document on Thursday.
"Accordingly, having regard to the objectives of legal certainty, transparency and the proper administration of judicial proceedings," the judges said they were exercising their authority to order the Registrar "to close the records of the Situation in Afghanistan".
The Chamber also noted that, although the investigation was authorised to cover alleged crimes committed in Afghanistan from May 1, 2003, and conflict-related crimes in other ICC member states from July 1, 2002, the prosecution had submitted only a limited number of applications under Article 58, all concerning the separate Situation in Afghanistan II, or the alleged crimes in Afghanistan since August 2021.
Afghanistan was invaded by US-led foreign forces in 2001, and the Western-backed administration in 2003 joined the Rome Statute.
The Taliban returned to power in August 2021 after the ouster of foreign forces from the war-torn nation, and subsequent meltdown of the Western-backed administration.
The prosecution told the Chamber it was pursuing three main lines of inquiry: alleged crimes by the Taliban against women and girls since August 2021; alleged crimes against other people, including persecution on political, ethnic and religious grounds; and alleged crimes committed by ISIS-K since 2016.
The decision also closes the investigation's line of inquiry into alleged crimes committed by the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISIS-K) since 2016.
The judges said, however, that the prosecution could seek new authorisation to investigate ISIS-K if it subsequently became able to pursue the inquiry effectively.
The judges clarified that the closure of the original investigation would not affect the prosecution's ongoing investigation into the Situation in Afghanistan II.
– Bernama-Anadolu
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gunung Kanthan limestone notch at critical risk of collapse, expert warns
Article:
IPOH: The limestone notch at Gunung Kanthan in Chemor, which houses the Dhamma Sakyamuni Cave Monastery, is in a critical and unsafe condition, with a risk of collapse at any time, a geoheritage expert has warned.
Emeritus Professor Datuk Dr Ibrahim Komoo said the formation was unsuitable for permanent habitation as it contained suspended limestone blocks without firm support.
He said the structure was not a cave in the conventional sense, but a natural formation created by the continuous dissolution of limestone over tens of thousands of years.
This process had weakened the natural cement holding the limestone blocks together through water seepage, increasing the risk of collapse.
"The condition at Gunung Kanthan is critical because limestone blocks are hanging without firm support.
"These internal processes cannot be seen with the naked eye. From a geological engineering perspective, it is impossible to predict precisely when a collapse will occur or guarantee the safety of the limestone structure," he said when met here.
Ibrahim said, in general, all cavities beneath limestone hills, including caves and notches, were unsafe for permanent habitation due to the risk of roof or structural collapse.
He said the collapse process could take a long time, but the exact timing remained unpredictable because changes within the rock structure were ongoing.
"Water seepage, particularly during heavy rain, can weaken the natural cement within limestone hills, making existing cracks increasingly unstable.
"Water entering rock fissures can also act as a lubricant, allowing limestone blocks to shift more easily and increasing the likelihood of collapse," he said.
He said collapses could occur during heavy rain or even minor tremors caused by quarry blasting or earthquakes.
Ibrahim said the notch at Gunung Kanthan had been formed by changes in groundwater levels, with slightly acidic water continuously dissolving the limestone over tens of thousands of years.
He said the formation had two layers of notches, separated by about five to six metres, while vertical cracks along the limestone walls showed evidence of previous collapses.
"I would not advise anyone to build a house or establish permanent accommodation in any cave anywhere in the world. Caves are not places for people to live," he said.
He said existing guidelines prohibited house construction within a distance of less than twice the height of a limestone cliff.
However, he said some parties had sought to revise the requirement to 1.5 times the cliff height.
The issue surrounding Gunung Kanthan has drawn renewed attention following controversy over the eviction and threatened demolition of the Dhamma Sakyamuni Cave Monastery to make way for quarrying activities.
The developments also prompted the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) to conduct a site visit and investigation into the matter recently.
In a separate development, a YTL Cement Bhd spokesman said Gunung Kanthan had been designated for cement production for 63 years, as part of the 45 limestone hill clusters in the Kinta Valley.
He said the limestone hill land had been legally leased by the state government to Associated Pan Malaysia Cement (APMC), a subsidiary of YTL Cement, with the formal endorsement and support of the federal government.
The spokesman said limestone karst formations carried inherent geological risks, including rockfalls and structural instability, requiring careful management, particularly in inhabited areas or near quarry operations.
"Geological assessments of the compartments at Gunung Kanthan have identified several safety concerns, including cracks and evidence of previous rockfalls.
"Although the Dhamma Sakyamuni Monastery receives relatively few visitors compared with public cave temples such as Sam Poh Tong in Ipoh, safety concerns cannot be taken lightly when lives are involved.
"Should an unfortunate incident occur, particularly one involving loss of life at the monastery as a result of quarry operations, APMC would remain responsible as the landowner, regardless of whether occupation of the area is legal or otherwise," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nearly 97,000 foreigners arrested for crimes since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities arrested 96,844 foreigners for various criminal offences nationwide between 2024 and September this year, reflecting a year-on-year upward trend.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the total comprised 33,136 arrests in 2024, before rising to 36,740 in 2025.
This represented an increase of 3,604 arrests, or 10.9 per cent, from the previous year.
"From January to September this year, 26,968 arrests of foreigners involved in criminal offences were recorded.
"The police will take stern action against any violation of the law and criminal acts involving foreigners in this country," he said in a statement today.
Khalid said the police has strengthened cooperation with other government agencies through integrated operations, intelligence sharing and more effective enforcement.
"In these actions, the police upholds the principle of equality before the law, whereby everyone, regardless of status, position or nationality, is subject to the laws of the country," he said.
The public and local communities are urged to continue acting as strategic partners by channelling information on criminal activities to the authorities to aid crime prevention and maintain public safety and order.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three houses damaged in Nibong Tebal pre-dawn blaze
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Three single-storey houses were damaged in an early morning fire at Kampung Baru Sungai Kecil today.
No casualties were reported.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 4.10am.
"All occupants evacuated before firefighters arrived," he said in a statement.
John said the fire destroyed about 90 per cent of the second house, 60 per cent of the first, and 1 per cent of the third.
The fire was brought under control at 4.44am and fully extinguished at 6.20am.
The operation ended at 6.44am. The case has been handed over to the Fire Investigation Department to determine the cause of the blaze and the total losses incurred.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flood evacuees increase in Selangor, drop in Perak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees seeking shelter at temporary relief centres (PPS) increased in Selangor but declined in Perak as of 8am today.
In
Selangor
, flood evacuee numbers at seven temporary relief centres in Kuala Selangor rose to 1,498 people from 402 families this morning, up from 1,373 people from 369 families yesterday evening.
The Social Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal reported that the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang is housing 428 evacuees, followed by SK Dato' Maharaja Lela (393), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (311), Dewan Orang Ramai Bukit Kuching Tengah (123), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (122), SRA Batu 8 Ijok (71) and Dewan Komuniti Penyayang Tanjung Siam (50).
Meanwhile, in
Perak
, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district fell to 265 people from 74 families, down from 274 people from 79 families yesterday evening.
According to the State Disaster Management Committee secretariat, the PPS at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall is housing 246 evacuees from 70 families, while the remaining 19 evacuees from four families are sheltered at the MPTI Langkap Hall.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast rain this morning in Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Manjung, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak and Bagan Datuk, while thunderstorms and rain are expected across all 12 districts in the afternoon and evening. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asean leaders to review implementation of Myanmar Five-Point Consensus, chart way forward
Article:
MANILA: Asean leaders will review the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) on Myanmar at the 49th Asean Summit in Manila and adopt a decision to guide the bloc's future engagement with the country, Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Theresa P. Lazaro said.
She said the document, titled the Asean Leaders' Review and Decision on the Implementation of the Five-Point Consensus, would take stock of developments in Myanmar and assess progress in implementing the 5PC since the previous review.
Lazaro said the 5PC remained Asean's primary reference for addressing the situation in Myanmar and that the bloc had repeatedly called for its full and effective implementation.
"This is a message that I reiterated during my recent bilateral meeting with the Myanmar foreign minister on Oct 29.
"As such, concrete progress would ultimately depend on the action points that Myanmar would be keen to implement," she told Bernama in a written interview.
Adopted by Asean leaders in 2021, the 5PC calls for an end to violence, dialogue among all parties and the delivery of humanitarian assistance, among other measures.
Lazaro said Myanmar had established an Asean Affairs Committee.
"It is our hope that the creation of this Committee would lead to substantive progress in the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus," she said.
On humanitarian access, Lazaro, who also serves as Asean's special envoy on Myanmar, said a mission she led in October had launched a month-long aid operation expected to reach more than 11,000 households in Kayin, northern Shan and southern Shan states.
The operation focused on communities that had yet to be reached by the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre).
During the mission, she said, the Asean Monitoring Team and representatives from the embassies of Asean member states and Japan distributed rice, family kits and personal hygiene kits.
"Moving forward for the duration of my term as Special Envoy, I will continue to advocate for expanded access, particularly to those areas and communities who need it the most," she said.
The Philippines, as Asean Chair for 2026, will host the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits in Manila from Nov 15 to 17.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will lead Malaysia's delegation to the meetings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Over 500 tourism operators under scrutiny, dozens offering umrah packages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 500 companies and individuals suspected of operating tourism businesses without valid licences are being monitored by the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry, with dozens offering umrah packages.
A check on the ministry's website found that dozens of entities on its list of those under investigation for violating the Tourism Industry Act 1992 (Act 482), as at Oct 15, were offering umrah packages, while others were promoting various domestic and international travel services, including trips to Europe.
The offences identified include violations of Section 21, involving the provision of tour guide services, and Subsection 5(2), which prohibits individuals or companies from operating tourism businesses without a valid licence.
Other violations involve Regulation 6(i), (ii) and (iii), which requires licensed operators to refund customers immediately, in accordance with agreed terms, in the event of changes to or cancellations of tourism contracts, such as flight schedule cancellations.
Through its watchlist, the ministry aims to alert the public while publicly identifying individuals and companies under investigation. Some are issued initial warnings, with enforcement action taken against those who continue to flout the law.
In a response to Berita Harian, the ministry said that up to October this year, two licensed companies had their licences suspended, while three had their licences revoked.
It said 12 entities had also been issued compounds for conducting tourism activities without valid licences.
"The ministry lists unlicensed operators on the watchlist on its portal. Intelligence, enforcement and advocacy efforts are also carried out continuously to ensure action is taken against unlicensed parties and to warn the public against dealing with them.
"At the same time, it continues to collaborate and engage with licensed industry players to ensure they comply with the legislation, standards and quality desired by Motac and Act 482".
On enforcement efforts to curb unlicensed tourism services, the ministry said its Tourism Licensing and Enforcement Division conducted operations, intelligence gathering and surveillance at all entry points into the country, including Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminals 1 and 2.
The operations are conducted aggressively, with a focus on popular tourist destinations nationwide.
It said intelligence gathering and inspections at both KLIA terminals had uncovered various offences, including entities offering tour and umrah packages without valid ministry licences.
Other offences included individuals providing tour guide services without valid licences, as well as private, commercial and e-hailing vehicles transporting tourists without tourist vehicle licences issued by the Land Public Transport Agency (Apad).
"The frequency of the ministry's enforcement operations at airports and other entry points is varied and not fixed to prevent offenders from detecting operational patterns.
"The ministry also works with KLIA management and other enforcement agencies through intelligence sharing and coordination of enforcement actions already taken."
The ministry said it collaborated with several enforcement agencies, including Apad, the Road Transport Department (RTD), the Immigration Department and tourism industry associations, to maximise action against those violating Act 482 and other relevant laws.
"Upon conviction, offenders may face imprisonment, a fine, or both, or be issued a compound, depending on the nature of the offence.
"Licences may also be suspended or revoked, in addition to fines, imprisonment or compounds.
"Action against licensed operators who breach regulations is ongoing, but the ministry's priority is to address unlicensed operators," it said.
On the growing number of umrah agencies operating without valid licences, the ministry said such offences fell under Subsection 5(2) of Act 482.
Those found guilty may face imprisonment of up to 10 years, a fine of up to RM500,000, or both, or a compound of up to RM250,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cast your ballots early before it rains, Ab Rauf tells Melaka voters [WATCH]
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh has urged voters to head to polling centres early today, citing forecasts of rain in the afternoon.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said voters should take advantage of the morning hours to cast their ballots, although arrangements had been made to assist them should it rain later.
"I hope voters will come out as early as possible this morning, as the weather forecast indicates that it may rain in the afternoon.
"However, we have made the necessary arrangements to assist voters in the event of rain," he said after casting his ballot at SK Jeram here.
Ab Rauf, who is also the incumbent Tanjung Bidara assemblyman, arrived at the polling centre with his wife, Datin Seri Zuriyah Ab Aziz, at about 8.30am.
On the voting process, Ab Rauf said he was satisfied with the arrangements made by Election Commission personnel, describing the process as orderly and convenient for voters.
"I can see that the EC officers are carrying out their duties in an orderly manner, and the arrangements have made it easier for voters to cast their ballots," he said.
He also thanked Melakans, particularly voters in Tanjung Bidara, for turning out to fulfil their voting responsibilities.
"Let us all remember to fulfil our responsibility today," he said.
Ab Rauf said he was also pleased with the morning turnout after being informed that more than 500 voters had arrived at the polling centre.
He is defending the Tanjung Bidara seat against Pakatan Harapan candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: 9.42 per cent turnout recorded as of 9am
Article:

ordinary voters
in the Melaka election had cast their ballots as of 9am today.

70 per cent turnout

Title: Anwar to lead Malaysian delegation at 49th Asean Summit in Manila
Article:
MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to arrive here today to lead the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which run from tomorrow until Tuesday.
Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony said the prime minister's participation reflects Malaysia's commitment to playing an active role in shaping Asean's direction across political and security, economic, and socio-cultural pillars.
"This summit provides a strategic platform for Malaysia to engage directly with leaders of Asean member states and dialogue partners, fostering dialogue on pressing shared challenges while strengthening bilateral ties in addressing regional issues," he told Malaysian media here.
Abdul Malik said Anwar will be accompanied by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, alongside Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
[[nid:1577232]]
"Tomorrow, the prime minister is scheduled to attend the 49th Asean Summit, comprising the plenary and retreat sessions, as well as three engagement sessions with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean Youth.
"The following day (Monday), Datuk Seri Anwar will join four summits with dialogue partners, namely the 29th Asean-China, 16th Asean-United Nations (UN), 6th Asean-Australia and 27th Asean-Republic of Korea summits," he said.
Anwar is scheduled to return to Malaysia on Monday afternoon to receive French President Emmanuel Macron for an official visit the next day.
He will return to Manila later that evening to attend the 12th Asean-United States (US) Special Summit and a gala dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
Anwar is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings with his Asean counterparts on the sidelines of the summits.
Meanwhile, Mohamad will lead the Malaysian delegation for several meetings on Nov 17, including the 29th Asean Plus Three (APT) Summit, the 4th Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Leaders' Meeting, the 29th Asean-Japan Summit, the 23rd Asean-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit.
In total, the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits comprise 10 summits, three engagement sessions and one leaders' meeting.

Title: US recalls over 720,000 BMW vehicles over fire risk, urges owners to park outside
Article:
NEW JERSEY: United States (US) safety regulators have advised owners of 720,796 BMW vehicles to park outside and away from buildings as an electrical fault could cause a fire, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported, citing recall documents.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said the recall involves a water pump electrical connector that may allow water to enter and cause a short circuit.
"Owners are advised to park their vehicles outside and away from structures until the recall remedy is completed," the agency said in a Nov 12 letter acknowledging BMW's recall.
The campaign replaces a 2024 recall covering the same vehicles.
Owners who had their vehicles repaired under that campaign will need the new remedy as well, NHTSA said.
BMW said in its filing that material degradation at the connector could allow moisture to enter the pump, increasing the risk of overheating and, in rare cases, a fire.
The earlier repair involved installing a protective shield to divert fluid away from the connector, inspecting the connector and wiring, and replacing damaged components where necessary.
However, a review in January identified further cases of overheating or thermal overload in vehicles that had already received that repair.
Subsequent testing found embrittlement and cracks in the connectors, according to BMW's account of its investigation.
BMW decided to launch the new recall on Oct 28 and submitted its report to NHTSA on Nov 4.
As of its decision date, the company was aware of approximately 10 US incidents that were, or might be, related to the defect. It said it had received no reports of related accidents or injuries.
The recall covers certain 2012–2016 3 Series, 5 Series and Z4 vehicles; 2012–2015 X1s; 2013–2017 X3s; 2015–2018 X4s; and 2016–2018 X5 xDrive40e models.
Also affected are certain 2014–2016 2 Series Coupes, 3 Series Sportswagons, 328xi Gran Turismos, 4 Series Coupes and Convertibles, along with 2015–2016 2 Series Convertibles and 4 Series Gran Coupes.
The repair remains under development and will be performed free of charge at authorised BMW centres.
Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed in December, NHTSA said.
Vehicle identification numbers covered by the recall, numbered 26V733, are expected to become searchable on the agency's website from Dec 25. — BERNAMA

Title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
Article:
WASHINGTON: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.
Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran – but he is not expected to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine, US officials said.
The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.
"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," Wales said.
One of the major conflicts dominating Trump's second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.
"I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin," a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.
Washington has a "whole other track" of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn't seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there," the official added.
Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won't be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.
Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday – their fourth meeting since the US president's return to power last year.
But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.
Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump's meetings with Xi, the officials said.
"The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip," a second US senior official said.
The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.
"We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration... and we don't expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we're there," the second official said.
Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit before heading to Shenzhen.--AFP

Title: Bus, container truck collide head-on in India, killing 23
Article:
NEW DELHI: A head-on collision between a container truck and a passenger bus killed at least 23 people, including three children, in eastern India on Friday, a police official told AFP.
The crash took place on a highway bordering Kaziranga National Park in the northeastern state of Assam.
The road is a designated animal corridor, where strict speed limits are in place.
"The total number of casualties is 23," said Swapneel Deka, the local district police chief.
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said he was "deeply distressed by the tragic accident."
"The scale of this loss has shaken all of us, and my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one," Sarma said on X.
India, with a population of 1.4 billion, recorded more than 183,000 road traffic deaths in 2025, or over 500 a day, according to the roads ministry.
Many accidents are linked to inadequate road infrastructure, poorly maintained vehicles and exhausted drivers, according to official data.--AFP

Title: Melaka polls: From morning jog straight to polling station for 80-year-old voter
Article:
MELAKA: At 80, retired civil servant Jusop Karim remains committed to exercising his right to vote, making a stop at SK Seri Duyong here after his morning jog and breakfast today.
Jusop said he had decided to visit the polling centre before proceeding with his other activities for the day.
"I went for my morning jog and stopped for a drink before coming here to vote.
"I am already 80 and have experienced several elections, but I am still excited to fulfil my responsibility as a voter," he told reporters after casting his ballot.
On the contest in Duyong, Jusop described the competition among the candidates as close, based on the information he had received.
However, he hoped that a candidate who had close ties with the local community would win.
"I do not mind who wins. What matters is that whoever is elected fulfils their responsibilities as a people's representative," he said.
Meanwhile, a check at SK Seri Duyong found that voters had begun queuing outside the school as early as 7am, ahead of the polling centre opening at 8am.
The incumbent Duyong assemblyman, Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abd Halem, who is defending the seat for Barisan Nasional, is facing Pakatan Harapan candidate Poo Long Suan.
The Election Commission's electoral roll records 26,528 eligible voters in Duyong, an increase of 8,291 from the 18,237 recorded in the 2021 state election.

Title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf arrives at SK Jeram to cast his vote [WATCH]
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh arrived at SK Jeram here about 8.30am to cast his vote in the Melaka election today.
Ab Rauf, who is also the incumbent Tanjung Bidara assemblyman, arrived at the polling centre wearing a batik shirt.
Upon arrival, he took time to greet voters who were there to cast their ballots and pose for photographs with them.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman is defending the seat in a straight fight against Pakatan Harapan candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri.
Tanjung Bidara has 15,003 registered voters.

Title: Melaka polls: Elderly couple up at 5am to cast votes
Article:
MASJID TANAH: An elderly couple who woke up about 5am to prepare for polling day were among the first voters to arrive at SK Jeram here this morning.
Liew Chee Phin, 66, and his wife, Tan Siw Choo, 62, from Taman Seri Aman reached the polling centre at 7.20am, well before it opened, to fulfil their voting responsibilities in the Melaka election.
Liew said they had set off after breakfast, with the polling centre about 2km from their home.
The father of three said he wanted to complete the voting process early as he had to open his shop in Masjid Tanah about 9am.
He said arriving early had become a habit whenever elections were held.
"Whenever there is an election, I always come early. I thought I would be able to have my identity card checked earlier this time too.
"Even so, I will wait because I want to fulfil my responsibility as a voter," he said.
For Rohana Yasin, 46, arriving early was also a matter of managing her time before reporting for work in Batu Berendam.
She said she did not want the distance to her workplace to prevent her from exercising her right to vote.
"That is why I came early to cast my vote.
"I have to reach work by 9.45am at the latest, so I need to hurry because the journey to my workplace is quite far.
"I thought I would be allowed to vote earlier, but it turned out that I had to wait until 8am," she said.
Rohana said she hoped to complete the voting process as quickly as possible to reach work on time.

Title: Ex-Nvidia CEO misled top lawyer on affair with Chinese businesswoman, sources say
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the company's leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters.
Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on condition of not quoting verbatim from the messages. The news agency is the first to report on this correspondence.
On Thursday, Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, a spectacular fall from the chip industry's heights where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent boom in artificial intelligence.
He apologised in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company.
His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International, whom the US was investigating for potentially spying for China.
Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share a last name but are not related.
The New York Times earlier this week reported Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, and Reuters reported on Thursday that Huang had another intimate relationship with a different Nvidia employee.
Teter did not respond to a request for comment. Wagonfeld did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A representative for ex-CEO Huang and an Nvidia spokesperson declined to comment.
A phone call and email to contact information listed on a business card for Alice Huang went unanswered.
During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders' attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate, the people said, speaking on the condition of anonymity.
Reuters only reviewed messages from the exchanges in October, not the ones from last year.
In two separate messages in October, Huang told Nvidia leaders, including Teter and Wagonfeld, that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers.
In other messages, Huang affirmed the routine nature of his interactions with Megaspeed.
Nvidia's Huang also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said.
That article had prompted Jensen Huang to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about their interactions, which he did not describe as an affair, the people said.
Ultimately, neither Nvidia nor Huang filed a lawsuit against the paper.
A spokesperson for the New York Times said the paper received no legal demand.
It is unclear when his relationship with Alice Huang became intimate. Photos posted online and verified by Reuters show them together in the US, China and elsewhere, dating as far back as December 2023.
On Nov 10, the independent members of Nvidia's board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after the New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Huang's relations with Alice Huang, as well as US authorities' suspicions that she was spying for China.
Beijing has denied she is a spy.
Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government.
Jensen Huang said in an interview with Bloomberg published on Oct 29 that the US government had not informed him about its suspicions regarding Alice Huang.
Nvidia's stock has fallen more than 30 per cent since its Oct 6 closing high, erasing more than $1.8 trillion from its market capitalisation. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC warns of scammers after 61 held for impersonating officers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The public have been advised to verify the identities of those claiming to be Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) officers before sharing personal information or making financial transactions.
This was following the arrest of 61 people suspected of involvement in a fraud syndicate.
The MCMC said it had taken note of reports on the arrests, involving people suspected of impersonating its staff during a police operation in Selangor.
The commission warned the public against falling victim to scams involving the misuse of its officers' names and identities.
"The public is urged to verify such claims through official channels before sharing personal information or making any financial transactions," it said in a statement.
The MCMC said such impersonation could threaten public safety and undermine public trust.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested over suspicious suitcase near KLCC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police arrested a 40-year-old man over a suspicious suitcase found at a bus stop near Suria KLCC in Jalan Ampang last night.
Dang Wangi district police chief assistant commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police received information about the discovery of the object at 7.17pm.
He said following this, a team comprising personnel from the Bomb Disposal Unit, K9 Unit and Kuala Lumpur Police Forensics Unit was dispatched to the scene to conduct checks and secure the area.
"Checks confirmed that there was no bomb threat inside the suitcase, and the suspect has since been detained to assist in investigations," he said in a statement.
Earlier, several posts about the situation outside the shopping mall went viral on social media, including the Threads application, showing the presence of policemen and vehicles.
The posts also showed traffic congestion and the closure of the road at the building's main entrance, causing concern among the public.
In this regard, Ahmad Azwan advised the public against speculating or spreading unverified information to avoid disrupting the investigation.
Those with information can contact Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2146 0522, Dang Wangi police headquarters control centre at 03-2600 2222, or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: 240 polling centres across state open simultaneously at 8am [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 240 ordinary polling centres, with 1,213 polling streams, for the 16th Melaka state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, allowing voters cast their ballots and elect a state government for the next term.
The Election Commission (EC) said a total of 675,166 ordinary voters were eligible to cast their ballots to elect representatives for the 28 state constituencies, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent.
Polling today is scheduled to continue until 6pm, following the end of the 14-day campaigning period at 11.59pm last night.
Overall, a total of 687,697 registered voters are eligible to vote in this election, including 12,531 military personnel, their spouses and police personnel who had cast their ballots during early voting on Tuesday.
Early voting, which involved 31 polling centres, recorded a physical turnout of 9,417 voters, or 94.96 per cent of the 9,917 eligible voters, while another 2,614 voted by post.
A total of 79 candidates from various political parties and independents are contesting the 28 state seats in this election, following the nomination process on Oct 31.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) has the highest number of candidates at 24, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Bersatu (seven), Perikatan Nasional (PN) (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one) and three independent candidates.
The election was called following the dissolution of the 15th Melaka State Legislative Assembly on Sept 23, with the consent of Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the 15th Melaka State Election held on Nov 20, 2021, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while PH secured five and PN two. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amazon fires: Brazil's Pará state declares 120-day emergency amid severe drought
Article:
BRASÍLIA: A northern Brazilian state has declared an environmental state of emergency due to hundreds of forest fires in the Amazon basin amid a severe drought linked to the El Nino climate phenomenon.
Since the start of November, the state of Para has already recorded more than 5,000 fires, almost as many as during the entire month of November 2025, according to satellite data from the National Institute for Space Research.
Nearly 700 fires were active in the last 48 hours.
The emergency measure announced Thursday is to last 120 days and bans the use of fire to clear pastureland and mobilizes additional resources to extinguish fires and prevent new outbreaks.
The Brazilian Amazon is affected by El Nino, the name given to the warming of an equatorial region of the Pacific Ocean, a climate phenomenon that raises temperatures and causes droughts. It is expected to become the most powerful ever recorded this year, experts say.
The drought in Para, which has 8.7 million inhabitants, is severe and the "parched vegetation is facilitating the spread of fire and threatening populations, forests and productive activities," the state government said.
Manaus, located in the neighbouring state of Amazonas, closed schools in early October due to the health risks posed by the smoke from hundreds of fires burning near urban areas.
The Amazon is the largest tropical forest in the world, and its conservation is essential to slowing global warming. In 2024, the Brazilian Amazon recorded a record number of forest fires.
This year is expected to be particularly severe, with a peak forecast for December. - AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cheaper flights home for Sarawak polls? Abang Johari fears bribery claims
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 14 — The Sarawak caretaker administration is cautious about proposals for state-owned carrier AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd (AirBorneo) to offer special airfare discounts to voters travelling home for the 13th Sarawak Election, warning that such incentives could be misconstrued as electoral bribery.
Caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said that while the administration was open to facilitating travel for Sarawakians, any fare reductions must comply with election laws and avoid giving rise to allegations of vote-buying.
“You see, if you give them a special discount, people can interpret it as a certain incentive.
“We have to look at the legal definition,” he told reporters after officiating at the send-off ceremony for AirBorneo’s inaugural Kuching-Jakarta flight at the Kuching International Airport yesterday.
He was responding to questions on whether the state government would consider directing AirBorneo to introduce additional airfare discounts to encourage out-of-state voters to return home and cast their ballots.
Abang Johari said initiatives intended to help voters could be portrayed negatively by political opponents and critics, with state-subsidised travel potentially framed as an attempt to influence votes.
“Nowadays, people will twist the narrative and ask: ‘Why is the government giving incentives for votes?’ If we sponsor the flights, some may claim it amounts to bribery.
“We have to be very careful because there are quarters who will spin this,” he said.
He acknowledged that airfares typically rise in December due to the year-end peak travel season, but said AirBorneo already offered fixed-rate fares that provided an affordable option for Sarawakians returning home.
“December flights are indeed very expensive, which is why voters should remember they can utilise AirBorneo.
“With fixed fares at just over RM300, they can already return home affordably without needing a special sponsorship that risks being misinterpreted,” he said.
The 13th Sarawak Election will see all 82 seats in the Sarawak Legislative Assembly contested following the dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly on October 26.
The Election Commission issued the writ of election on November 6, with nomination set for November 28, marking the start of the 14-day campaign period ending on December 11.
Early voting will be held on December 8, ahead of polling day on December 12.
More than two million registered voters are eligible to vote, with a simple majority of 42 seats needed to form the next state government. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak school alert leads to arrest of palm worker, 28, after Year Six girl found pregnant
Article:
KABONG, Nov 14 — Sarawak police have arrested a 28-year-old man after a 12-year-old Year Six pupil was found to be pregnant, Berita Harian reported last night.
The case came to light when the girl’s mother took her to school to inform the management of the pregnancy, Saratok district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mathew Manggie said.
“The victim admitted to having sexual relations three times in mid-June,” he was quoted as saying.
The woman also reportedly told the school that she wanted her daughter to stop schooling so she could marry the suspect.
The school head instead referred the matter to the district education office, which directed that a police report be lodged as the victim is underage.
Initial investigations found that the suspect, an oil palm plantation worker, had known the girl since mid-2025, Mathew said.
“The victim realised she was pregnant about a week before telling her mother on November 11,” he added.
Acting on the police report, a team from the Saratok district criminal investigation division arrested the suspect at a longhouse in Kabong, he said.
Mathew said the case is being investigated under Section 376 of the Penal Code.
The offence of rape is defined under Section 375 of the Penal Code, which treats sex with a girl under 16 as rape regardless of consent, while Section 376 provides for imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
