Title: Anwar receives 11 outstanding asnaf pupils from Kinabatangan who achieved national, international success
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday received a visit from 11 outstanding asnaf pupils from Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Singgah Manis in Kinabatangan, Sabah, accompanied by seven of their teachers, at Kompleks Seri Perdana.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was impressed by the perseverance of the pupils and teachers, who had achieved various successes at state, national and international levels despite coming from a rural school.
“I advised the children to remain diligent in their pursuit of knowledge and to have the courage to chase their dreams. When they achieve success, remember to help their parents and give back to the community,” he said.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to the school’s teachers for their commitment to educating, guiding and instilling confidence in the pupils to reach greater heights.
“The achievements of SK Singgah Manis pupils strengthen our resolve to ensure that every child, regardless of how far away they live, has equal opportunities to learn, develop their talents and achieve their aspirations,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Minister: Govt exploring Sijil Turath Malaysia implementation next year to give pondok students university pathway
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 14 — The government is exploring the implementation of the Sijil Turath Malaysia, expected to be introduced next year, to give official recognition to pondok and turath students and open pathways for them to pursue university studies and build careers.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the move follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement when tabling Budget 2027, which also includes the establishment of the Malaysian Pondok and Turath Advisory Council.
“This certificate is generally the government’s effort to see how pondok and turath institutions are recognised, and it can serve as a qualification enabling students to enter university and build their careers.
“So we want to see how best to develop this Sijil Turath Malaysia. Just as we have the Sijil Tahfiz Malaysia, we will now have the Sijil Turath Malaysia, Insya-Allah (God willing),” he told reporters after opening the International Sama’ Jami’ al-Tirmizi and al-Syamail al-Muhammadiyyah 2026 event here last night.
The 11-day event, which runs from today until Nov 23, gathers international Islamic scholars and local intellectuals, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim scheduled to attend the closing ceremony.
Elaborating on the certificate, Zulkifli said it is intended for local pondok and turath institutions, as well as any institution wishing to adopt the syllabus recognised under the Sijil Turath Malaysia, on par with the current implementation of the Sijil Tahfiz Malaysia.
Earlier, in his opening speech, Zulkifli said the initiative is part of the government’s efforts to build a more structured and systematic Islamic scholarly ecosystem, in line with the Budget 2027 announcement to establish the Malaysian Pondok and Turath Advisory Council.
He said the government wants pondok and turath institutions to continue preserving the authenticity of their learning traditions, the strength of the ‘talaqqi’ method, the teacher-student bond and mastery of classical Islamic texts (kitab turath), which form part of Islamic scholarly heritage.
“This effort also paves the way for educational recognition, infrastructure development, and mastery of digital skills and artificial intelligence (AI), while opening up future opportunities for students,” he said.
In a related development, he said religious affairs agencies have agreed to continue the project to publish an updated translation of Sahih al-Bukhari, involving improvements to translation accuracy, spelling, terminology and technical layout across all eight volumes.
“This publication is not merely a reprint, but also includes a digital format through the MyHadis portal alongside physical copies for official distribution,” he said. — Bernama

Title: AirBorneo takes off for Jakarta: Kuching direct flights from RM399
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 14 — Sarawak’s state-owned carrier AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd (AirBorneo) has launched direct flights between Kuching and Jakarta, establishing a new air link between Sarawak and Indonesia’s capital.
The inaugural flight, MY396, departed Kuching International Airport yesterday and arrived at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport Terminal 3 to a traditional water salute, completing the journey in under two hours.
AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said Jakarta was the airline’s first destination in Indonesia and its third jet route since services began in July.
“We see it as a link between neighbours rather than simply a market we fly into, and we hope it serves business travellers, families and visitors in both directions.
“We are very glad to bring Kuching and Jakarta a little closer,” he said, adding that the airline’s immediate priority was to operate the route reliably and grow it sustainably.
The flight was sent off at the Kuching International Airport by caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.
AirBorneo said the new service was expected to support stronger ties between Sarawak and Indonesia in business, tourism and healthcare by providing a direct connection without the need for transit through a third city.
For businesses, investors and official delegations, the route is expected to facilitate trade, investment and bilateral partnerships between Sarawak and Jakarta.
It is also expected to encourage two-way tourism, giving Indonesian visitors easier access to Sarawak’s Unesco World Heritage sites, rainforests and cultural festivals, while providing Sarawakians with a direct link to Jakarta’s food, fashion, creative and lifestyle attractions.
The service is also expected to benefit medical travellers, particularly patients and family members coming to Sarawak for specialist treatment, second opinions, diagnostic screening or planned procedures.
AirBorneo said avoiding connecting flights would make travel easier for elderly passengers and those recovering from medical treatment.
The Kuching-Jakarta route operates three times a week, on Mondays, Fridays and Sundays, using a Boeing 737-800 aircraft with 12 Business Class and 150 Economy Class seats.
Flight MY396 operates from Kuching to Jakarta, while the return service is numbered MY397.
One-way all-in fares from Kuching start at RM399 for Economy Class and RM888 for Business Class.
Fares from Jakarta start at 1.75 million rupiah (RM402) and 3.88 million rupiah (RM892) respectively.
The fares include checked baggage, seat selection and in-flight meals.
AirBorneo said tickets were available exclusively through its official website, www.airborneo.com, mobile app, ticketing offices and accredited travel agents to ensure fare transparency and protect passengers from unauthorised third-party mark-ups.
Travellers can book flights directly or arrange holiday packages through accredited travel partners.
Customers in Indonesia can also pay in Indonesian rupiah through local digital payment channels. — The Borneo Post

Title: Civic duty knows no bounds: Visually impaired voter travels from Ipoh to vote in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — A 23-year-old visually impaired voter travelled from Ipoh, Perak, to Melaka today to exercise his democratic right, making the long journey to fulfil his civic duty.
Muhammad Adam Iskandar Muhammad Rayme, a voter in the Bukit Katil state constituency, said this was his second time voting, having first cast his ballot at the age of 19 with his mother accompanying him.
“This time, I came with my younger sibling and we arrived at Sekolah Kebangsaan Dato’ Demang Hussin as early as 7am.
“The process was smoother and easier as I could draw on my previous experience,” he told Bernama.
He also commended election workers for their readiness and willingness to assist him, despite the challenges he faced as a visually impaired voter.
“We depend on the person accompanying us, but the voting process was easier and more orderly,” said the Ipoh-based massage therapist. — Bernama

Title: MB: Johor govt hopes filling of posts at Hospital Pasir Gudang can be expedited as nurses, specialists in short supply
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 14 — The Johor State Government hopes the filling of posts at Hospital Pasir Gudang (HPG) can be expedited to ensure sufficient manpower in line with the hospital’s expanding service capacity.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said 1,276 of the 2,271 posts allocated to HPG had been filled as of November 6, or 56 per cent.
He said the fill rate for nursing posts remained low at 40 per cent, while that for medical specialists stood at just 39 per cent.
“The Johor State Government will continue to champion manpower needs and the welfare of healthcare workers to provide the best healthcare services for Bangsa Johor, InsyaAllah,” he said in a Facebook post.
Onn Hafiz said the state government has also implemented various initiatives to support smooth hospital operations, including bringing in the fully state-funded Southern Volunteers (SV) Healthcare.
The initiative is aimed at streamlining hospital operations, easing workloads and safeguarding the welfare of doctors, nurses and healthcare workers.
Meanwhile, he said 239 of the 304 beds at HPG, or 79 per cent, were operational as of November 1.
The capacity is scheduled to increase in stages to reach 100 per cent by March 2027.
Previously, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad was reported as saying that the Ministry of Health (MOH) remains committed to ensuring HPG operates optimally according to its scheduled phases to safeguard quality healthcare for the people of Johor. — Bernama

Title: Penang Education Dept to probe allegation that teacher slapped, pinched SPM candidate
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 14 — The Penang State Education Department is investigating allegations that a teacher repeatedly slapped and pinched an Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidate, causing bruises, and verbally humiliated the student at a school here.
Penang Education Department director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said the department received a complaint regarding the incident and instructed the District Education Office to conduct an investigation and submit recommendations on further action and resolution.
“The district education office also met with the student and the student’s family this evening. The department will extend its full cooperation to the authorities involved in this matter,” he told Bernama when contacted last night.
The allegations went viral on social media following a post by the student’s parents, who appealed to Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek to look into the incident involving their child, a student at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Penanti in Kubang Semang here.
According to the post, the student was allegedly slapped and pinched repeatedly, resulting in bruises, and verbally humiliated by a teacher for failing to achieve good results in the Principles of Accounting subject.
The student’s parents also claimed that the incident had affected their child’s self-confidence, causing the student to become afraid of attending school and express reluctance to sit for the SPM examination, which is scheduled to begin next week.
Mohamad Dziauddin said the department’s immediate priority was to provide socio-emotional counselling and support to the student to help with preparations for the examination.
He also urged all parties to work together in supporting the development of a safe educational environment for both students and teachers, particularly as 2026 SPM candidates enter the final stage of their examination preparations.
He said everyone’s support was important in ensuring that a positive atmosphere and perception of the education system were maintained. — Bernama

Title: She knew and chose silence: Kuching mother gets five years’ jail for allowing teen daughter’s sexual abuse
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 14 — A 52-year-old woman was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment by the Sessions Court here for allowing her teenage daughter to be sexually abused by her 77-year-old grand-uncle and failing to lodge a police report despite having knowledge about the incident.
Judge Noorhisham Mohd Jaafar imposed the sentence after the woman pleaded guilty to an offence framed under Section 31(1)(b) of the Child Act 2001.
The court ordered her jail term to take effect from the date of her arrest, on October 21 this year.
Noorhisham also ordered her to undergo rehabilitative counselling throughout her imprisonment period under Section 26(1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act (SOACA) 2017.
The judge further ordered her to be placed under police supervision for two years under Section 27(1) of the same Act.
According to the charge, the woman had allowed her daughter to be sexually abused at a house in Padawan on October 11 this year.
Based on the facts of the case, the incident occurred when the 77-year-old grand-uncle visited the house to collect fertiliser and asked the girl for assistance.
The teenager was home alone when the man allegedly groped her breasts and private parts before kissing her on the mouth.
She tried to push him away, but was unsuccessful.
The man also told her to keep the incident a secret.
The following day, the victim attended school as usual, but a friend noticed she was crying and informed the school counsellor.
The counsellor subsequently contacted the victim’s parents and arranged a meeting to discuss the incident.
However, the parents decided against lodging a police report after discussing the matter, as they did not want to pursue the case as it involved a family member and also due to fear of being blamed by other relatives.
In a separate proceeding before Noorhisham, the girl’s grand-uncle pleaded not guilty to a charge of physically sexually assaulting her.
He was charged under Section 14(a) of SOACA 2017, read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act.
The court denied him bail and fixed this December 11 for case management.
Meanwhile, the girl’s father, who was also charged under Section 31(1)(b) of the Child Act 2001 in connection with the same offence, pleaded not guilty before Sessions Court Judge Musli Ab Hamid.
Musli also denied him bail and fixed December 14 for case management.
The victim is expected to be referred to Sarawak General Hospital for a medical examination and to the Protector at the Kuching Welfare Department for assessment.
* If you are experiencing sexual violence, the following hotlines offer free and confidential support: Talian Kasih at 15999 or WhatsApp 019-2615999 (24/7); All Women’s Action Society at 016-2374221 / 016-2284221 (9.30am-5.30pm); and Women’s Aid Organisation (WAO) at 03-30008858 or SMS/WhatsApp TINA 018-9888058 (24/7)
** If you suspect child abuse, call the following hotlines for free and confidential support: Talian Kasih at 15999 or WhatsApp 019-2615999 (24/7); Talian BuddyBear at 1800-18-2327(BEAR) (noon-midnight daily); and One Crisis Centre (24/7) Wilayah Persekutuan at 03-26155555 (Kuala Lumpur General Hospital), 03-61454333 (Sungai Buloh Hospital) or 03-83124200 (Putrajaya Hospital).
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Afiq Safly Nor Kazly prosecuted all three cases, while none of the three individuals were represented by counsel. — The Borneo Post

Title: Flood evacuees increase in Selangor, drop in Perak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The number of flood evacuees seeking shelter at temporary relief centres (PPS) increased in Selangor but declined in Perak as of 8am today.
In SELANGOR, flood evacuee numbers at seven temporary relief centres in Kuala Selangor rose to 1,498 people from 402 families this morning, up from 1,373 people from 369 families yesterday evening.
The Social Welfare Department’s InfoBencana portal reported that the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang is housing 428 evacuees, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (393), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (311), Dewan Orang Ramai Bukit Kuching Tengah (123), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (122), SRA Batu 8 Ijok (71) and Dewan Komuniti Penyayang Tanjung Siam (50).
Meanwhile, in PERAK, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district fell to 265 people from 74 families, down from 274 people from 79 families yesterday evening.
According to the State Disaster Management Committee secretariat, the PPS at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall is housing 246 evacuees from 70 families, while the remaining 19 evacuees from four families are sheltered at the MPTI Langkap Hall.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast rain this morning in Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Manjung, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak and Bagan Datuk, while thunderstorms and rain are expected across all 12 districts in the afternoon and evening. — Bernama

Title: Ab Rauf and Adam Adli cast ballots as Melaka heads to polls
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh cast his vote for the 16th Melaka state election at 8.38am today.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, who is also the incumbent of Tanjung Bidara state constituency, arrived to vote at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Jeram in Masjid Tanah, Alor Gajah, accompanied by his wife, Datin Seri Zuriyah Ab Aziz, who also cast her vote at the same location.
Speaking to the media afterwards, Ab Rauf expressed his hope that all voters in Melaka would come out to fulfill their duty of electing their respective representatives today.
In this state election, Ab Rauf faces a straight fight against Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who is making his electoral debut.
During the 15th Melaka state election, Ab Rauf won a three-way contest with a majority of 364 votes, defeating PH candidate Zainal Hassan and Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin of Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Meanwhile, the acting chairman of the Melaka PKR State Leadership Council, Adam Adli Abdul Halim, was among the first voters to arrive at the polling station at SK Dato’ Demang Hussin, Bukit Katil, to fulfill his duty as a voter in the constituency.
Higher Education Deputy Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim votes in the 16th Melaka State Election at Sekolah Kebangsaan Demang Hussin November 14, 2026. — Bernama pic
Adam Adli, who also serves as the Deputy Minister of Higher Education, arrived around 7.45am, joined the queue with other voters before entering the polling station.
The Bukit Katil state constituency is seeing a four-way contest between the incumbent, Adly Zahari who is also the Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif (Perikatan Nasional/PN), Dr. Aliza Che Amran (Parti Bersama Malaysia), and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
Meanwhile, Adly, who also serves as the Deputy Minister of Defence, is expected to cast his vote at 4.00 pm, following his inspection of the voting process in the constituency.
At SJK© Notre Dame, Melaka DAP publicity secretary Kerk Chee Yee fulfilled his duty as a voter for the Kota Laksamana state constituency at approximately 8.20am.
The PH candidate for Ayer Keroh state seat urged all voters in Melaka to come out and exercise their duty as early as possible today.
“I would like to remind voters to check their designated polling station locations beforehand to avoid any confusion, especially those who might still be referring to old information,” he said.
Kerk, 34 who has held the Ayer Keroh seat for two terms is facing a four-way contest against Datuk Seri Michael Gan (PN), Muhammad Muhaimin Lau Abdullah (Parti Bersama Malaysia), and Mohd Hamnaim Mohamad (Bersatu).
In the Machap Jaya state constituency, PH candidate Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin cast her vote at 8.10am at SJK(c) Machap Umboo, Alor Gajah.
This constituency is seeing a three-way race between Lim, the incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem (Barisan Nasional/BN), and Prasanth Kumar Brakasam (Parti Bersama Malaysia).
Meanwhile, Ngwe arrived to cast his vote at SK Rendah Agama Jaim, Kampung Ayer, Machap, at 9.10am.
Get the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election at https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Man gets 12 months' jail, RM250,000 fine for Quran desecration in Pahang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — A man was sentenced to 12 months in prison and fined RM250,000 by the Kuantan Sessions Court in Pahang for desecrating the Quran and posting grossly offensive content on social media in February.
Judge Harmi Thamri Mohamad imposed the sentence yesterday after S. Vikneswaran, 21, a former university student, pleaded guilty to both charges.
The court ordered the prison sentence to take effect from November 12, with an additional 12 months’ imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine.
The judge said the sentence was meant not only to teach the accused a lesson but also to warn the public against committing similar offences.
Lawyer Muhammad Amirull Afiqq Mohamad Lokman, who represented Vikneswaran, applied for a stay of execution of the prison sentence pending an appeal, citing his client’s scheduled psychiatric treatment appointments.
Pahang State Prosecution director Mohd Sabri Othman opposed the application, arguing that there were no special circumstances to justify the court granting the defence’s request.
As a result, the accused began serving his prison sentence yesterday.
According to the charge, the man was accused of desecrating an object held sacred by Muslims, namely the Quran, with the intention of insulting Islam at Jalan Gambang, Taman Seri Mahkota, here, at about 1.30pm on February 22.
He was charged under Section 295 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison term of two years, a fine, or both.
The second charge alleged that he had knowingly used the Threads account “ryandaselva” to post a grossly offensive communication with the intention of causing distress to others.
The charge was brought under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and is punishable under Section 233(2) of the same Act by a maximum fine of RM500,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, with a further fine of RM5,000 for each day the offence continues after conviction.
The incident came to light after the accused’s father, the complainant, was contacted by his daughter on February 24 and told about a viral video on Threads showing the accused’s actions.
The complainant then contacted the accused about the viral video, and the accused admitted he was the person shown in it.
Investigations found that the act was committed at a house in Taman Seri Mahkota Aman, here.
The accused was arrested at 3.30pm on February 25, and police seized his mobile phone and a copy of the Quran for investigation.
Social media analysis and reports from telecommunications companies confirmed that the account and phone numbers used belonged to the accused and his family. — Bernama

Title: No bomb threat: Man arrested after suspicious suitcase near KLCC sparks road closure, social media frenzy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Police arrested a 40-year-old man to assist in investigations into the discovery of a suspicious-looking suitcase at a bus stop near the Suria KLCC shopping mall in Jalan Ampang here last night.
Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police received information about the discovery of the object at 7.17pm.
He said following this, a team comprising personnel from the Bomb Disposal Unit, K9 Unit and Kuala Lumpur Police Forensics Unit was dispatched to the scene to conduct checks and secure the area.
“Checks confirmed that there was no bomb threat inside the suitcase, and the suspect has since been detained to assist in investigations,” he said in a statement.
Earlier, several posts about the situation outside the shopping mall went viral on social media, including the Threads application, showing the presence of police personnel and vehicles.
The posts also showed traffic congestion and the closure of the road at the building’s main entrance, causing concern among members of the public.
In this regard, Ahmad Azwan advised the public against speculating or spreading unverified information to avoid disrupting the investigation.
Members of the public with information related to the incident can contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522, the Dang Wangi district police headquarters control centre at 03-2600 2222, or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Woman found strangled in Banting, police arrest son to aid probe
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 14 — A woman in her 50s was found dead, believed to have been strangled, at a house in Banting, Kuala Langat, yesterday.
Kuala Langat district police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said police were alerted to the incident at about 1 pm.
“Initial examinations found that the victim was believed to have been murdered by strangulation, with pressure applied to her neck.
“Following this, police arrested the woman’s son, in his 20s, who is suspected of being linked to the incident,” he said in a statement.
He said the motive for the incident was still under investigation. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Members of the public with information about the incident are urged to contact the Kuala Langat District police headquarters operations room at 03-31872222 or the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: MCMC warns public over scams impersonating its officers after 61 arrested in Selangor
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) takes a serious view of the misuse of its officers’ names and identities to deceive the public, particularly for fraudulent purposes.
The MCMC said in a statement today that it had taken note of reports on the arrest of 61 individuals suspected of involvement in a fraud syndicate that impersonated its officers during a police operation in Selangor.
“The MCMC views seriously any misuse of its officers’ names and identities to deceive the public, especially in fraudulent activities that could threaten public safety and undermine public trust,” it said.
The commission also pledged full cooperation with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) in the ongoing investigation, including by providing relevant information.
The MCMC advised the public to remain vigilant when receiving calls or messages from individuals claiming to be its officers.
“The public is urged to verify such claims through official channels before sharing personal information or making any financial transactions,” it said. — Bernama

Title: No free pass for foreigners who break the law, IGP says as arrests since 2024 near 97,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Police will take firm action against any violation of the law and criminal conduct involving foreigners in Malaysia, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has said.
He said 96,844 foreign nationals were arrested for various crimes from 2024 to September 2026, based on Criminal Investigation Department (CID) statistics.
“PDRM will take firm action against any form of violation of the law and criminal conduct involving foreigners in Malaysia,” Mohd Khalid said in a statement in Malay today, using the abbreviation for the Royal Malaysia Police.
He said arrests of foreign nationals numbered 33,136 in 2024 and rose to 36,740 the following year, an increase of 3,604 arrests or 10.9 per cent.
A further 26,968 arrests were recorded from January to September 2026, he said.
He said the police would also strengthen synergy with other government agencies through integrated operations, intelligence sharing and more effective enforcement.
“PDRM adheres firmly to the principle of equality before the law, and every individual, regardless of status, position or nationality, is subject to the laws of the country,” he said.
“Any act that violates the law will not be compromised and will be dealt with through firm enforcement action in line with the legislation in force,” he added.
He also urged the public to continue acting as the police’s strategic partners by channelling information on criminal activities to the authorities.
The statement comes days after a police officer’s hand was severed at the wrist by an allegedly unstable foreign man in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, last Wednesday before the man was shot dead.
The 26-year-old lance corporal from the Gombak district police headquarters had his right hand reattached at Hospital Kuala Lumpur, and is reported to be able to move several fingers.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the suspect lived in the apartment but was not a registered tenant, and police are investigating his mental health.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail directed police to carry out a thorough investigation, while Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim condemned the attack.
Yesterday,
Utusan Malaysia
reported that police were directed to act firmly and not compromise on any violation of the law, particularly involving foreigners.
In June, the government vowed to step up enforcement against foreign nationals who abuse business licences and visas, amid growing public complaints.

Title: Anwar to lead Malaysian delegation at 49th Asean Summit in Manila, says envoy
Article:
MANILA, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to arrive in Manila tomorrow to lead the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17.
Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony said Anwar’s participation at the highest level reflects Malaysia’s commitment to continuing its active role in shaping Asean’s direction across political and security, economic and socio-cultural aspects.
“This summit provides a strategic platform to engage directly with leaders of Asean Member States and Dialogue Partners, fostering dialogue on pressing shared challenges while strengthening key bilateral ties,” he told Malaysian media at a press conference here.
Abdul Malik said Anwar will be accompanied by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
On Sunday, the Prime Minister is scheduled to attend the plenary and retreat sessions of the 49th Asean Summit, as well as Asean leaders’ engagement sessions with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth.
On Monday, he is scheduled to attend Asean summits with China, the United Nations (UN), Australia and South Korea before returning to Malaysia in the afternoon.
Abdul Malik said the return is to allow Anwar to receive French President Emmanuel Macron for an official visit on the morning of November 17.
“The Prime Minister is scheduled to return to Manila on the afternoon of November 17, 2026, to attend the Asean-United States Special Summit and a dinner hosted by the President of the Republic of the Philippines,” he said.
Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan will lead the Malaysian delegation to several meetings and summits on November 17 in the Prime Minister’s absence, including the 29th Asean Plus Three Summit, the 4th Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Leaders’ Meeting, Asean summits with Japan and India, and the 21st East Asia Summit.
Abdul Malik said Anwar is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings with his counterparts from Asean member states on the sidelines of the summit.
He said the summit will be preceded by four ministerial-level meetings on November 14, including the Extended Informal Consultation on the Implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.
The other three meetings are the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, the 32nd Asean Political-Security Community Council Meeting and the 39th Asean Coordinating Council Meeting.
“Overall, the programme comprises 10 summits, three engagement sessions and one leaders’ meeting,” he said.
He said Malaysia’s participation in the summit is vital to safeguard national interests and strengthen the country’s active role in shaping Asean’s future direction. — Bernama

Title: PKFZ says Speedmatrix didn’t sign, Port Klang land lease won’t go ahead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd’s proposed lease of land in Port Klang will not proceed after the company did not sign a letter of offer that has since expired, Port Klang Free Zone Sdn Bhd (PKFZ) said today.
In a statement today, PKFZ said it was responding to recent reports concerning Speedmatrix.
“PKFZ remains resolute in preventing the Free Zone from being used for unlawful activities,” said its chairman Lim Lip Eng, who is also Kepong MP.
PKFZ said Speedmatrix sought to lease a parcel of land within the free zone in July.
It said the letter of offer it issued contained terms and conditions, including “an express prohibition on the export of computer chips without prior approval from the relevant authorities”.
PKFZ said Speedmatrix did not execute the letter of offer within the stipulated validity period, and the offer expired in early November.
It said it formally notified Speedmatrix on November 13 that the letter of offer had lapsed and that the proposed lease would not proceed.
“Through due diligence, risk assessments, company background checks and stringent terms and conditions, PKFZ is committed to addressing risks before businesses commence operations within the zone,” Lim said.
The statement did not elaborate on the reports it referred to.
Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng, who is Port Klang Free Zone chairman, said on November 14, 2026 that Speedmatrix’s bid to lease land in the free zone did not go ahead as the offer had lapsed, amid scrutiny of its parent company Megaspeed over whether restricted Nvidia chips were routed through Malaysia. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Yesterday, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) said it never cleared Megaspeed or Speedmatrix, and that Speedmatrix is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia.
Miti is working with the Customs Department to check whether any chips brought into Malaysia were re-exported.
Speedmatrix is the Malaysian unit of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia customer.
The
New York Times
reported that Speedmatrix bought at least US$4.8 billion of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026.
Megaspeed has denied diverting chips illegally to China.
Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, is alleged by the US to have been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to gather information on Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang; Beijing has rejected the claims.
The two Huangs are not related to each other by blood or marriage.
Alice has been reported to be one of several women to have had an affair with Jensen.
Jensen told Nvidia employees on November 8 that he had been unfaithful to his wife, and the company’s board opened an independent investigation.
But Nvidia has also described his contacts with Alice as ordinary customer interactions.
The Nvidia co-founder resigned as chief executive last Thursday, with chief financial officer Colette Kress appointed interim chief executive.

Title: Anwar extends condolences to former deputy minister Zahidi's family
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin, who passed away yesterday.
In a Facebook post, Anwar prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the deceased’s sins and shower his soul with mercy.
“May his family be granted strength and remain steadfast in facing this great trial,” he said.
Meanwhile, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil also expressed his sorrow over the passing of the former Padang Besar Member of Parliament.
“On behalf of everyone at the Communications Ministry, I would like to extend my condolences to the entire family and friends of the deceased.
“May they be granted strength, patience and fortitude in facing this loss,” he said.
He also called on the public to pray that the deceased’s soul would be showered with mercy, his sins be forgiven and that he would be placed among the faithful.
Zahidi’s remains were laid to rest at the Bayan Lepas Islamic Cemetery in Penang after Isyak prayers. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia: Wind convergence to bring thunderstorms, heavy rain to most peninsular states from Nov 15 to 17
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in most states in Peninsular Malaysia from November 15 to 17, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
Its director-general, Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, said this was based on an analysis of the latest weather forecast models, which indicated that a convergence of winds was expected during the period.
“This situation could bring thunderstorms accompanied by heavy rain and strong winds over a longer duration in most states in Peninsular Malaysia,” he said in a statement posted on MetMalaysia’s Facebook page.
In this regard, Mohd Hisham advised the public to regularly refer to the department’s website at
www.met.gov.my
and its official social media platforms, as well as download the myCuaca application for the latest and verified information.
In a related development, MetMalaysia has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong wind warning for five states until 11 o’clock last night.
The warning covers Kota Tinggi and Kluang in Johor, as well as Hulu Perak and Kuala Kangsar in Perak.
Similar warnings have also been issued for Padang Terap, Sik and Baling in Kedah, and Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Besut in Terengganu.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Kapit, Bintulu, Mukah, Sibu, Sarikei, Betong (Kabong and Saratok), as well as Miri (Subis, Miri and Beluru). — Bernama

Title: PM urges Melaka voters to reject exploiters of religion, corrupt individuals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people of Melaka to use their ballots in the state election tomorrow to reject those who exploit religion for political gain, as well as individuals involved in corruption.
In a Facebook post tonight, Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, said Melaka voters had an opportunity to send a strong message and become a beacon of hope for those who wanted to see the country free from corruption.
“Over the past few days, we have witnessed the true face of a so-called ‘unity’. For the sake of votes and power, they have stooped so low as to exploit religion by issuing fatwas legitimising support for corrupt individuals, demonising their opponents and even equating the choice of who to vote for with the obligation to perform ablution.
“Tomorrow, the people of Melaka have an opportunity to send a strong message through the ballot box. Reject those who exploit religion and those who hide behind the guise of championing the interests of the community but, in reality, are glorifying corrupt individuals,” he said.
Anwar said the attitude of remaining silent and tolerating corruption had damaged the country for far too long and must be brought to an end through the voters’ choices.
“We must put an end to it at the ballot box tomorrow. Save Melaka. Save the country. Vote for HARAPAN,” he said.
A total of 675,166 voters are eligible to cast their ballots in the 16th Melaka State Election, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent. — Bernama

Title: Former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Zahidi Zainul Abidin dies at 65
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 14 — Former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin died yesterday and was laid to rest at the Bayan Lepas Islamic Cemetery after Isyak prayers last night.
News of his passing was shared by former Perlis Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim, who extended his condolences to the deceased’s family.
In a Facebook post, Shahidan, who is the Member of Parliament for Arau, said he was deeply saddened by his friend’s passing.
“It is with sadness that I inform you of the passing of the former Padang Besar Member of Parliament, a man who had rendered invaluable service. His passing is a great loss to us all.
“Innalillahi wa inna ilaihi raji’un. Throughout his life, he had dedicated himself to the people of Padang Besar. May Allah SWT forgive all his sins, accept his good deeds and sacrifices, and place his soul among the righteous,” Shahidan said in the post.
Earlier, a condolence poster announcing Zahidi’s death went viral on social media, accompanied by details of the funeral prayer and burial arrangements, which were held at Masjid Bayan Lepas.
The news was subsequently confirmed by the deceased’s younger brother, Zafruddin Zainul Abidin. Zafruddin said his elder brother died at about 5pm yesterday.
He was reported to have said that he had been informed of his brother’s deteriorating health since Wednesday and that Zahidi had been receiving treatment at a private hospital in Penang. He was believed to have been suffering from kidney failure and required dialysis.
Zahidi, 65, served as the Padang Besar Member of Parliament for two terms after winning the seat in the 13th and 14th General Elections.
He held several key positions in national politics and administration, including Deputy Communications and Multimedia Minister under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) administrations from March 2020 to November 2022.
In Perlis politics, he served as a state executive councillor from 1999 to 2006 during Shahidan’s tenure as Menteri Besar. He was also the Beseri state assemblyman from 1999 to 2008. — Bernama

Title: Melaka votes today: 79 candidates seek mandate from 675,166 electors
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — After the Melaka State Election campaign ended at midnight last night, the power to choose now shifts to 675,166 ordinary voters who will determine the fate of 79 candidates competing for 28 state assembly seats today.
From speeches to face-to-face meetings, various strategies were deployed by political parties throughout the 14-day campaign to convince the people that they are the best choice to voice and fulfil the aspirations of the residents of this historic state.
Yesterday, Election Commission (EC) deputy chairman Dr. Azmi Sharom aimed for a voter turnout percentage of around 70 per cent in this state election, with the full results expected to be known before midnight.
The EC had previously announced 240 polling centres with 1,213 voting streams opened throughout the state from 8 am to 6 pm, to enable registered voters to cast their votes.
Overall, a total of 687,697 registered voters are eligible to vote in this Melaka State Election, including 12,531 military personnel and their spouses, as well as police officers and their spouses who did so through early voting on Tuesday.
The early voting, which involved 31 polling centres, recorded 9,417 or 94.96 per cent of the 9,917 voters who physically cast their votes on that day, while 2,614 others voted by post.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) fielded the most candidates, with 24 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 23 candidates, Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Bersatu (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one) and three independent candidates.
This election is held following the dissolution of the 15th Melaka State Assembly on September 23 after receiving the consent of the Yang Dipertua Negeri Melaka, Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the 15th Melaka State Election held in November 2021, BN won 21 out of 28 state seats, with PH (five) and PN (two).
Get the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election at
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: 240 polling centres across state open simultaneously at 8am for 675,166 Melaka voters
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — A total of 240 ordinary polling centres, with 1,213 polling streams, for the 16th Melaka state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, allowing voters cast their ballots and elect a state government for the next term.
The Election Commission (EC) said a total of 675,166 ordinary voters were eligible to cast their ballots to elect representatives for the 28 state constituencies, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent.
Polling today is scheduled to continue until 6pm, following the end of the 14-day campaigning period at 11.59pm last night.
Overall, a total of 687,697 registered voters are eligible to vote in this election, including 12,531 military personnel, their spouses and police personnel who had cast their ballots during early voting on Tuesday.
Early voting, which involved 31 polling centres, recorded a physical turnout of 9,417 voters, or 94.96 per cent of the 9,917 eligible voters, while another 2,614 voted by post.
A total of 79 candidates from various political parties and independents are contesting the 28 state seats in this election, following the nomination process on October 31.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) has the highest number of candidates at 24, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Bersatu (seven), Perikatan Nasional (PN) (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one) and three independent candidates.
The election was called following the dissolution of the 15th Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23, with the consent of Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the 15th Melaka State Election held on November 20, 2021, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while PH secured five and PN two.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB moves to back Tuanku Muhriz and avert government shutdown, says source
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has taken steps this week to affirm the status of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar, in a development that may finally see an end to the state’s seven-month-long constitutional crisis.
The state government is currently in virtual paralysis, with Ismail the sole member of the executive, as his executive council members were earlier dismissed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar for breaching their oath of office and loyalty.
Ismail urgently needs to convene a state assembly meeting to approve the state Budget, or face the possibility of an unprecedented halt to government and administrative services if funding is not approved by the legislature.
But he needs the consent of Tuanku Muhriz for the state assembly to meet.
A source told
Malay Mail
that Ismail met earlier this week with Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad, the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal, and presented him with a letter withdrawing objections to Tuanku Muhriz’s position as state ruler.
It is understood the move is also supported by the ten former members of the state exco who were sacked by Tuanku Muhriz.
Syed Danial is expected to inform the Conference of Rulers of Ismail’s decision.
Sources said Ismail is now expected to seek an audience with the state ruler to express his loyalty and seek consent for the sitting of the state assembly.
Ismail had allegedly written a letter to the Conference of Rulers in September declaring Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the “new” Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
This followed an earlier attempt to install Tunku Nadzaruddin as the state’s new ruler, which has not been recognised by Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s federal government.
Amid the crisis in Negeri Sembilan, the Conference of Rulers met last month without Tuanku Muhriz.
In a statement after the meeting, the Malay Rulers warned against outside interference and attempts to politicise the crisis in Negeri Sembilan.
The Rulers said that contradictory and irresponsible statements will only exacerbate the situation, heighten tensions, confuse the public and tarnish the dignity of the royal institution.
Ismail was sworn in by Tuanku Muhriz as Menteri Besar on August 2, following a state election that saw Barisan Nasional win 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan 11, and Perikatan Nasional seven.
The assembly sitting was originally scheduled for October 16, but was subsequently moved to November 26 to coincide with the planned tabling of the state’s Budget the next day.
But the dates remain subject to consent from Tuanku Muhriz.
The relationship between Tuanku Muhriz and Ismail hit a low point last month when the state ruler publicly reprimanded the latter.

Title: Prisons Dept: Najib’s nearly eight-hour outing on Friday was not only for prayers, included hospital check-up and counselling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Prisons Department has clarified that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s nearly eight-hour absence from his house arrest residence on Friday was not solely for Friday prayers, as earlier reported.
The department had taken note of media reports that Najib was out of his residence for almost eight hours on November 13.
“His movements on that day began at 10.25am until 6.25pm and did not involve only performing Friday prayers as reported,” the department said in a statement late last night.
According to the department, Najib attended a follow-up medical appointment at the orthopaedic department of Hospital Kuala Lumpur.
He then performed Friday prayers at the Kajang Prison mosque.
The department said he also attended a Quran study session with an
ustaz
from the Islamic Development Department at Kajang Prison.
It added that he later attended a counselling session with a psychology officer at the prison.
“After all these matters were completed, he was taken home from Kajang Prison at 5.50pm and arrived at his house in Jalan Langgak Duta at 6.25pm,” it said.
The department stressed that “every movement of his is carried out based on the matters and needs that have been determined, and is subject to standard operating procedures, house arrest conditions, and the control and supervision of the Malaysian Prisons Department”.
It said religious activities, healthcare, and rehabilitation and intervention programmes are among the aspects given attention in the management of an individual serving a sentence.
The department added that it would continue to ensure all related matters are carried out in an orderly and professional manner, in compliance with the rules in force.
Chinese-language newspaper Sin Chew Daily had yesterday reported that Najib left his home at about 10.28am and returned at about 6.27pm on Friday, in an outing that lasted nearly eight hours.
Najib was convicted of abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million of SRC International Sdn Bhd funds.
He is serving the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, following a conditional royal pardon granted in September.
Under the Pardons Board’s conditions, he is barred from engaging in political activities, making media statements or appearing on social media.
He is also prohibited from leaving the gazetted premises without written permission, although prison officers are permitted to escort him for Friday prayers.

Title: Melaka polls become test of Najib house arrest row, with GE16 battle lines emerging
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Melaka voters head to the polls today for a state election that began as a contest over development, governance and political alliances, but has become increasingly dominated by the controversy surrounding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest.
The issue has given Barisan Nasional (BN), particularly Umno, an opportunity to present Najib’s transfer from prison to home detention as the fruit of its efforts and a promise delivered to its supporters.
Meanwhile, Pakatan Harapan (PH) has used the controversy as a rallying point to challenge Umno and mobilise voters unhappy with the decision.
Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has argued that the conditional pardon granted to Najib under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution must be respected, warning that protests against the decision could amount to challenging the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional authority.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke – who resigned as transport minister after the High Court allowed Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year SRC International Sdn Bhd sentence under house arrest – has urged Melaka voters to channel their dissatisfaction through the ballot box.
The Najib controversy featured prominently at the rival coalitions’ final campaign rallies on Thursday night, with both PH and the BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) alliance making the former prime minister’s house arrest a central theme in their appeals to voters, albeit from opposing positions.
At PH’s grand finale mega ceramah in Hang Tuah Jaya, several coalition leaders, including Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa and DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo, raised Najib’s SRC case and the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) scandal while urging Melaka voters to send a message through their ballots.
Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim (on stage centre) stumps for Pakatan Harapan at the coalition’s grand finale ceramah in Bukit Baru, Melaka on November 12, 2026. — Bernama pic
At the BN-PN grand finale mega ceramah in Bukit Katil on the same night, leaders from Umno, PAS and their allies defended the royal decision on Najib’s house arrest while turning their criticism towards DAP over its opposition to the arrangement.
Criticising Loke’s resignation as transport minister, Parti Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said PN and BN respected the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s decree and would strongly oppose anyone who challenged it.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki also accused DAP of questioning the King’s authority.
PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man also weighed in on the controversy, saying decisions by the Pardons Board and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong should be supported.
He questioned Loke’s resignation, saying the prime minister had issued a statement the same night that he had yet to accept the resignation letter.
Tuan Ibrahim said that if DAP’s stand was truly one of principle, the party should go further.
“We challenge all Cabinet members to resign, not just the party’s secretary-general,” he said.
Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi (left) takes a selfie with Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man at the BN-PN grand finale ceramah in Paya Rumput, Melaka on November 11, 2026. — Bernama pic
Anwar has since said he had yet to accept Loke’s resignation letter as he wanted to discuss the matter with him first.
“For now, he wants to take a short break, and that is fine. But we need to discuss his resignation again,” the prime minister said at PH’s grand finale in Bukit Baru on Thursday night.
He also praised Loke as a clean and hardworking minister, and questioned why critics wanted a good minister to step down while poor performers stayed on.
The contrasting positions have turned the final stretch of campaigning into a wider political argument over Najib, the royal prerogative of mercy and the relationship between Umno and DAP, despite both parties being part of the federal government.
The dispute also offers an early glimpse of the battle lines that could emerge ahead of the 16th general election.
Bread-and-butter issues pushed to the sidelines
Political analyst Azmi Hassan, a senior fellow at the Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research, said Umno and PH had each used the controversy to their advantage, seeking to turn it into sympathy and motivation among their supporters.
He said Umno was telling its supporters it had “worked very hard” to bring Najib home, while DAP would stress that it was still protesting the decision.
However, Azmi said the controversy had overshadowed the bread-and-butter issues in the parties’ manifestos, especially in the final days of the campaign.
“I think the Melaka voters have been deprived of the real issue, the bread and butter issue,” he told
Malay Mail.
Traditional trades such as Samsudin Abdul’s bullock-cart rides for visitors in Telok Mas reflect the local livelihood concerns Melaka voters say matter to them, from jobs to tourism. — Bernama pic
Azmi said both BN and PH could benefit from the controversy by encouraging supporters who might otherwise have stayed home to turn out and vote, although it was difficult to determine which side stood to gain more.
Healso predicted that voter turnout could reach between 70 and 75 per cent, due to the mobilisation generated by the Najib issue.
“As I see it, the voter turnout, I think can reached 70 per cent, 75 per cent just because of this particular issue,” he said.
Original battleground
Before the controversy took centre stage, BN and PN had sought to make economic growth and continuity the centrepiece of their joint campaign under the Muafakat Melaka arrangement.
Their manifesto promises to attract RM30 billion in investments, provide free domestic water to households using less than 20 cubic metres a month and freeze quit rent increases for five years.
Caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh who is from Umno, has also defended his administration’s record, claiming that BN had fulfilled 97 per cent of its promises in the 2021 state election manifesto.
Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), although a PN component party, is contesting seven seats under its own logo, outside the BN-PN pact.
PH, meanwhile, has sought to position itself as a credible alternative administration, challenging BN’s record on governance and delivery while pitching its own plans for economic opportunities, youth employment and tourism development.
Its manifesto,
Aspirasi Melaka Rumah Kita
, includes proposals for more transparent administration, a Smart Melaka transformation and allocating 30 per cent of local authority work contracts to young people.
These competing pitches now risk receiving less attention as the campaign becomes increasingly framed around the national controversy.
Political analyst Amir Fareed Rahim, strategic director of consultancy KRA Group, had previously described the campaign as relatively subdued and less confrontational than the Johor state election, with local economic concerns initially taking precedence over national political rhetoric.
He said voters were primarily concerned about jobs and living costs, as well as whether tourism was improving local livelihoods, the impact of coastal reclamation on fishing communities and how the state would address worsening traffic.
Election Commission staff prepare ballot boxes at SMK Ayer Keroh in Melaka ahead of the state election on November 14, 2026. — Bernama pic
However, Amir Fareed identified the controversy surrounding Najib’s house arrest as a possible factor affecting PH supporters’ motivation to vote during the second week of campaigning.
He also said PH had room to make gains, with Budget 2027 potentially providing a boost, although Parti Bersama Malaysia, which had been organising in Melaka even before the state assembly was dissolved, could draw support from the same pool of voters.
With 79 candidates contesting the 28 state seats, including 24 from PH, 23 from BN, 16 from Bersama, seven from Bersatu and five from PN, the outcome will also depend on turnout and whether supporters are willing to cross party lines or stay home.

Title: Designing the money part of Malaysia’s long-term care system: Economists share what to look out for
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — It may be “tricky” for Malaysia to figure out who or what will be paying for the long-term care and support of older Malaysians in their day-to-day life, an economist has said.
So what can Malaysia consider when designing a long-term care scheme?
Long-term care system: Tax-funded or insurance?
World Bank senior economist Matthew Dornan said there is “no easy answer” for how Malaysia would fund its long-term care system.
“I think the financing — it’s really important, nothing is going to happen without financing. But it’s also tricky and I think any path that Malaysia takes will be tricky,” he said at the recent National Long-Term Care Financing Dialogue 2026.
As people will always “undersave” or save less than what they actually need, Dornan said a mandatory long-term care system is necessary to share the risks or costs with others.
He said Malaysia could do it either through a tax-funded or mandatory insurance for long-term care, but both will come with its own challenges.
He cited Australia — which has a progressive income tax system and broad tax base — which primarily uses tax revenue for its long-term care costs.
For Malaysia, the obvious challenge if it were to opt for a tax-funded long-term care system is its fiscal space or low tax revenues, he said.
“So the government doesn’t have very much money basically. And so, you know, what do you need to fund a long-term care system using a tax basis?
“Well, you need fiscal reform. You need to boost your tax base, and/or you need to review and reform the subsidies that are in place, which is a very unpopular thing to do. So, you know, that’s really, really tricky,” he said.
As for the insurance option, he noted that countries such as Japan and Korea’s national long-term care insurance schemes still have tax-funded elements.
He said tax revenue plays an important role in those insurance schemes, as it also covers and supports the older generation which had not paid contributions to the insurance.
Dornan said Malaysia does not have a national health insurance system that a long-term care insurance could be built on.
He noted that building it on something like the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) system is also challenging as it does not cover everyone, and those unincluded will have to rely on the tax-funded system.
Among other things, he also said long-term care financing cannot be looked at in isolation, and that there is also a need to consider the entire pension system and people’s financial wellbeing as these are closely linked to each other.
Decide what kind of long-term care costs would be covered first
World Health Organization (WHO) senior health economist Debbie Muirhead agreed that all of the possible financing pathways for a long-term care system should be looked at, and said Malaysia may end up adopting a mixed system.
She said the first step when designing a long-term care system should be deciding what it would cover, as a country would then know “what it’s going to cost” to deliver those benefits.
After a country decides the “benefits package” or what long-term care costs it would cover, it could then have something realistic to start off with and to adjust.
She said the benefits package can be narrowed down in two ways: Either by narrowing or reducing the scope of services that would be covered, or by prioritising those with the greatest need for long-term care (either in terms of financial need or care needs).
She cited the WHO’s “Long-term care for older people: package for universal health coverage” guide which outlines core interventions that could be given priority, and said Malaysia could see if it fits the local context.
World Health Organization (WHO) senior health economist Debbie Muirhead said a country should start with identifying the benefits or long-term care services when creating its long-term care system, in order to know how much it would cost. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Noting the preference of older Malaysians to continue staying or ageing in their homes, she said this could involve working-age family members — who are providing unpaid care and lose out on pension benefits as they are not in jobs.
She said various factors could be looked at, such as whether a long-term care system should include any financial compensation or pension compensation for such unpaid carers who are saving the system money.
She said older people and their caregivers should be involved in discussions of what a long-term care system’s benefits package would cover “so that we know that it’s really meeting their needs”.
“Importantly though, a financing approach for a scheme should never be seen as the end in itself,” she said earlier, noting that governments should never lose sight of the need to have the right benefits and right incentives to deliver the desired outcomes for older people in the country.
Start small first, then add on
Muirhead said “starting small” with the benefits package would not only make a long-term care system affordable, but would also provide ongoing political capital when governments announce new expansions and additions to the package.
She said this would also prevent losing public trust.
“And the other thing is, if we promise things — entitlements in a package — and then we can’t afford to deliver it, that trust and public acceptability — and trust, that’s so important in something like long-term care — gets diminished as well. So, it’s always good to have that very considered approach about what we can forward,” she said.
File photo for illustration only. Debbie Muirhead said the World Health Organization (WHO) promotes age-friendly cities and communities, with the aim of enabling people to age healthily in place and to remain active. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Beyond just money: How to support ageing in place and being active within a community
Among other things, she noted that Malaysians’ life expectancy at birth in 2026 is at 75.5 years, but noted that healthy life expectancy in Malaysia has hovered around 65.5 years and that would mean Malaysians on average spend the last 10 years of their life in poor health.
She said there is a need to invest in healthier lifestyles and healthy ageing at an earlier age, including by having age-friendly cities and communities (with 11 cities in Malaysia participating to date in the WHO’s network of such communities).
She said there is a misconception that long-term care is only about getting care at institutional residential facilities, noting that WHO instead defines it as covering the whole range of services and supports “that people need to live with dignity, autonomy and participation in society”.
She stressed the importance of integrated care for older people, which does not only cover healthcare needs, but also covers social needs care.
This includes “social prescribing”, where healthcare workers connect older people to activities and services within their community, which Muirhead said could reduce loneliness and improve their wellbeing and mental health.
The dialogue was part of the National Conference on Ageing 2026 (NCA 2026), which was organised by Universiti Putra Malaysia’s Malaysian Research Institute on Ageing (MyAgeing) together with Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP), the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the Malaysia Caregivers Association (Kendana).

Title: PKR leaders slam Hadi over remarks comparing Muslim, non-Muslim leaders, question PAS ties with MCA, Gerakan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Several PKR leaders have criticised PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his remarks comparing Muslim and non-Muslim leaders, warning that religious sentiments should not be used to divide Malaysians for political gain.
PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said political differences should be debated based on policies and solutions to people’s problems rather than religious sentiments.
He described Abdul Hadi’s remarks during a Melaka state election campaign event yesterday as deeply disappointing, saying statements that hurt religious sensitivities and fuel tensions would only harm the country.
Abdul Hadi was quoted as saying that even the worst Muslim leaders governing a country would not be as oppressive as non-Muslims.
“As a religious figure with extensive knowledge, he should set an example in promoting good character and unity. Unfortunately, that knowledge is not reflected in the wisdom of his words,” Chang said in a statement today.
Chang, who is also Science, Technology and Innovation Minister, said Malaysia’s multiracial and multireligious harmony was essential to economic development, investor confidence and job creation.
He questioned whether the pursuit of political power should come at the expense of national unity and stability, stressing that Malaysia needed leaders who brought people together rather than divided them.
Meanwhile, PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh questioned how Abdul Hadi’s remarks aligned with opposition political cooperation in Melaka, particularly involving MCA and Gerakan in the campaign for Kelebang seat.
“Interestingly, the MCA president had spoken at the same campaign event, while Gerakan president Dominic Lau also appealed to Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional supporters to back a non-Muslim Gerakan candidate.
“This happened in front of a Malay-majority audience. So, how should Abdul Hadi’s remarks be interpreted in the context of their political cooperation?” said Fuziah, who is also Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister.
Fuziah also expressed support for Pakatan Harapan’s candidate for Kelebang, Farzana Hayani, saying that her links to the federal ruling coalition could help bring local concerns to the government’s attention regardless of race or religion.
Separately, PKR Youth (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim described Abdul Hadi’s remarks as extreme and prejudiced, warning that they could fuel religious hostility and undermine national unity.
He noted that it is all the more concerning that such a statement came from a senior political leader who possesses a background in religious education and wields significant influence within the Muslim community.
“Such a position and level of knowledge should be used to foster an understanding of Islam rooted in justice, wisdom, and noble character, not to cultivate the perception that a Muslim possesses an absolute moral superiority over followers of other religions, even when committing acts of injustice,” he said in a statement.
He said that the AMK views the attempt to weigh the severity of an injustice based on religious identity as a departure from the principle of justice, a fundamental tenet of Islamic teachings. Furthermore, it raises questions regarding the party’s sincerity in building political cooperation across racial and religious lines.
“Do such views also apply to the leaders of the MCA and Gerakan, who are PAS’s political partners? Or is this principle applied only when dealing with those who hold opposing political stances?” he asked.
As such, Muhammad Kamil urged Abdul Hadi to publicly clarify and retract his remarks, saying justice should apply equally regardless of race, religion or political affiliation.
He stressed that Malaysia’s future must be grounded in constitutional principles, respect for Islam as the religion of the Federation and the protection of religious freedom for all citizens.
“Justice does not discriminate based on the perpetrator’s skin colour, lineage, or religion; indeed, injustice must be opposed, even when committed by those of the same race, religion, or political persuasion,” he added.
Meanwhile, Sabah Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud described Abdul Hadi’s statement as extreme, out of bounds and completely unacceptable.
“Such remarks not only offend followers of other religions, but could also disrupt the harmony of Malaysia’s multiracial society, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, which have long lived in an atmosphere of mutual respect regardless of religion, race and culture.
“In Sabah, there is no place for politics that discriminates against followers of other religions, as religious differences are not a barrier to family ties, friendship and community life,” he said.
He said a family in Sabah can have members who practise different faiths, yet they still live in harmony and mutual respect.
Mustapha stressed that Islam teaches its followers to be just to all people regardless of religion, adding that a leader’s justice or tyranny must be judged by their actions and integrity, not the faith they profess.
“As a political leader and religious figure, Abdul Hadi should act responsibly and refrain from making statements that could arouse prejudice and undermine social harmony,” he said.
Mustapha urged Sabahans and all Malaysians, particularly the people of Melaka, to remain vigilant and reject political parties that preach hatred against followers of other religions. — Bernama

Title: HKL monitors cop after successful hand reattachment following Kepong machete attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL), is closely monitoring the recovery of a policeman whose hand was reattached following an attack on Wednesday (November 11).
HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K. Ragavan Nair said the policeman was referred to the hospital for specialist treatment and immediately taken to the Main Operating Theatre for surgery after thorough examination and assessment by a team of specialists.
He said the eight-hour surgery involved reattaching injured blood vessels and nerve structures, as well as restoring the anatomical structure of the affected hand.
“The surgery was led by HKL Upper Limb and Microsurgery subspecialists Dr R. Allan Ravi and Dr Aziz Sabbir Husain, in collaboration with the entire HKL Upper Limb and Microsurgery Unit team and the anaesthesiology team,” he said in a statement here today.
Harikrishna said the case involved a complex procedure requiring specialised expertise, advanced microsurgical skills and close multidisciplinary collaboration to ensure comprehensive and optimal treatment.
He added that HKL remains committed to providing high-quality treatment services through multidisciplinary expertise, technology and professional skills for the wellbeing of the community.
On Wednesday, the policeman’s right hand was severed at the wrist after he was attacked by a foreign man armed with a machete at a residential premises in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong. — Bernama
